div.head: CHn cor 3, 3.1
div.ab: Et si quis baronum uel aliorum hominum meorum filiam suam nuptum tradere uoluerit, siue sororem siue neptem siue cognatam, mecum inde loquatur. [3, 1] Sed neque ego aliquid de suo pro hac licentia accipiam, neque defendam ei quin eam det, excepto si eam uellet iungere inimico meo.

Et si quis baronum vel aliorum hominum meorum filiam suam nuptum tradere voluerit, sive sororem sive neptem sive cognatam, mecum inde loquatur, sed neque ego aliquid de suo pro hac licentia accipiam, neque defendam ei quin eam det, excepto si eam vellet iungere inimico meo.

And if any of my barons or my other vassals wishes to bestow in marriage his daughter or his sister or his niece or any [other] female relative he shall consult me on the matter, but I shall not take anything from him in return for my permission, nor shall I forbid him to bestow her in marriage, unless he desires to marry her to an enemy of mine.

Der Wille des Mädchens wird nicht befragt, nur der der Witwe (3, 3. 4); s. Gl Eheschliessung 16 p. t. Hier handelt es sich nicht, wie 3, 2, nur um die filia heres (die ihrem Manne ihres Vaters Lehn mitbringt); durch Vorversterben männlicher Erben des Vaters konnte sie nach der Heirat hæres werden. Wo man für Schwester, Nichte, Base Heiratslizenz des Lehnsherrn nachsucht, ist man statt ihres Vaters Vormund, das Mädchen Waise.—Der Singular steht für alle Töchter, wenn der Grundbesitz mehreren vererbte; Pol Mai II 273.—Die Rubrik, die Quadr II 2, o. I 544, zu diesem Satze setzt, betont die Bindung dieser Verheiratung an den Willen der Lehnsherren. Vgl. Gl Lehnwesen 6. 13

The girl’s wishes are not consulted, only those of the widow (3, 3. 4); see Gl Eheschliessung 16 p. t. Here it is not, as in 3, 2, only a question of the filia heres (who brings her father’s fief to her husband); through the prior death of her father’s male heirs she could become hæres after the marriage. Where the lord’s licence to marry is sought for a sister, niece or cousin, the petitioner is guardian in place of her father, and the girl an orphan.—The singular stands for all the daughters if the landed property passed by inheritance to several; Pol Mai II 273.—The rubric that Quadr II 2 (above I 544) places on this sentence stresses that such marriages were bound to the will of the feudal lords. Cf. Gl Lehnwesen 6. 13
loqui cum rege seit Domesdaybuch stereotyp: ‘mit oberster Verwaltungsinstanz verhandeln’, in Dingen, wo blosse Beamte oder Kommissare nicht zu entscheiden wagen; Freeman Nor. conq. V 46

loqui cum rege is a stock phrase from Domesday Book onwards: ‘to negotiate with the highest administrative authority’, in matters which mere officials or commissioners do not venture to decide; Freeman Nor. conq. V 46

Offenbar hatte also Wilhelm II. die Heiratslizenz verkauft. Diese bildete eine Geldquelle zwar schon unter Cnut (II 74, o. S. 213); aber nicht aus Agsächs. Brauche, sondern aus Französ. Lehnrecht stammt dieser fiskale Anspruch

Evidently, then, William II had sold the licence to marry. This was indeed already a source of money under Cnut (II 74, above p. 213); but this fiscal claim derives not from Anglo-Saxon custom but from French feudal law
